# CANDIDATE: ORATS_SKEW_STEEPEN_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A steepening put-call IV skew (ORATS 0DTE 25-delta put IV minus call IV > 0.025) signals elevated demand for downside protection, often preceding a short-covering rally when price breaks upward with volume. We expect to capture edge by entering long when this skew condition coincides with a strong intraday breakout above the opening range high on elevated volume, filtered by VIX < 22 and time-of-day (10:00-12:00 EST) to align with institutional flows.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** Trigger fires when all conditions are met on the same 5-minute bar:
- ORATS 0DTE 25-delta IV skew (put IV - call IV) > 0.025
- Close > opening range high (ORH)
- Volume > 2 × 20-bar average volume
- Close > 20-period EMA
- Time between 10:00-12:00 EST
- VIX < 22

**Exit:**
- Initial stop: midpoint of the opening range (chart-stop)
- Profit target: 2R (twice risk from entry to stop)
- After hitting 1R, trail remaining position with premium-stop of 12% (exit if premium drops 12% from its post-1R peak)
- Time stop: 15:50 ET (standard 0DTE exit)

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** Strategy assumes Safe account of $25K+ for full position sizing (qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline). Based on risk-rules.md, max risk per trade is 50% of equity; we target ITM-2/ATM 0DTE puts/calls with premium ~$1.00-$2.00, so 28 contracts risks ~$5,600-$11,200 per trade, requiring $11,200-$22,400 account for full size. $1K paper account would trade ~2-3 contracts (14% of headline).
2. **Sample bias:** Zero-sample hypothesis; no historical testing conducted. High overfit risk until validated. Selection method: purely theoretical based on ORATS skew literature and observed market microstructure.

   - Blow-up scenario: Regime shift where steepening skew no longer predicts upward breaks (e.g., sustained downtrend with persistent high skew)
